courses.subject: SEEM
courses.title: Advanced Data Science for Systems Engineering
courses.description: This graduate level course introduces the basic concepts of statistical pattern processing and machine learning algorithm. A particular focus is given on state-of-the-art machine learning techniques used in a set of application systems including but not limited to financial market models, pricing models, fraud detection, natural language processing, speech and audio technologies that are purposefully designed for the current SEEM research postgraduate students specializing in either of the two broad areas of information systems and operational research. This course is also available to undergraduate students of senior years with sufficient backgrounds in linear algebra, vector calculus, probability and statistics.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in SEEM MPhil/PhD programme and RPg programmes under Faculty of Engineering
courses.academic_group: Div of System Erg & Erg Mgt
courses.academic_org: Div of System Erg & Erg Mgt
courses.learning_outcomes:
Understand the basic principles of pattern classification and machine learning.
Understand Expectation Maximization as a general optimization technique.
Understand sequence modelling and representation approaches such as hidden Markov models and finite state transducers
Understand current sequence classification and prediction schemes such as feedforward neural networks and recurrent neural networks
Understand Bayesian learning techniques and Gaussian process to model uncertainty
Apply machine learning techniques to practical applications in application systems such as financial engineering and speech recognition
courses.course_syllabus: This graduate level course introduces the basic concepts of statistical pattern processing and machine learning algorithm. A particular focus is given on state-of-the-art machine learning techniques used in a set of application systems for systems engineering and engineering management, for example, stock price prediction and analysis, and fraudulent transaction detection. Topics to be covered include: Bayes decision theory; Supervised and unsupervised learning; Linear regression and linear classifiers; Fisher discriminant analysis, PCA, LDA, ICA and factor analysis; Gaussian mixture models; Expectation maximization; Markov models and sequence modelling; K-means clustering; Classification and Regression Trees; Non-parametric estimation; Single and multiple layer perceptron; Error back propagation; Gradient descent; Deep neural networks; Convolutional and recurrent neural networks; second order optimization; Bayesian learning for Classification and Regression; Gaussian Process; Bayesian and Gaussian Process deep neural networks; Deep sequence to sequence models; Weighted Finite state transducers etc.

courses.subject: SEEM
courses.title: Numerical Optimization
courses.description: This course is to teach students modern numerical optimization methods for large scale systems. Topics covered in this course include gradient method, subgradient method, proximal gradient method, Nesterov's acceleration technique, alternating direction method of multipliers, coordinate descent method, and stochastic / randomized algorithms. Applications of these optimization methods for solving problems in contemporary applications arising from big data analytics, machine learning, statistics, signal processing etc. will also be discussed.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in SEEM MPhil/PhD programme and RPg programmes under Faculty of Engineering
courses.academic_group: Div of System Erg & Erg Mgt
courses.academic_org: Div of System Erg & Erg Mgt
courses.learning_outcomes:
At the completion of this course, the student should
• familiarize with optimization algorithms for solving large scale optimization problems
• understand the convergence behaviors of different algorithms
• understand the capability of different algorithms
• be able to use learned algorithms to solve practical problems
courses.course_syllabus:
This course introduces modern numerical optimization methods and underlying theory for complex/large scale systems. Particular focuses will be given to direct search methods, various gradient methods, subgradient methods and acceleration techniques, stochastic/randomized algorithms, cutting plane methods and level function methods. It will also introduce fundamental theory of convex and quasi-convex optimization. At the end of the course, students are expected to apply the learned optimization methods to solve practical problems arising from areas such as big data analytics, machine learning, statistics and signal processing.

Syllabus (tentative)

1. Direct search methods
2. Convexity, quasi-convexity and Fenchel duality
3. Cutting plane method and level function method
4. Gradient method and quasi-Newton method
5. Subgradient and subgradient method
6. Proximal mapping and proximal gradient method
7. Accelerated proximal gradient method
8. Proximal point method and augmented Lagrangian method
9. Alternating direction method of multipliers
10. Coordinate descent method
11. Stochastic algorithms

• Individual meetings with students on course, especially on choice of term project topic

• D. Bertsekas, Nonlinear Programming, Athena Scientific, 1999
• J. Nocedal and S.J. Wright, Numerical Optimization, Springer, 2006
• Y. Nesterov, Introductory Lectures on Convex Optimization: A Basic Course, Kluwer, 2003

courses.subject: SEEM
courses.title: Optimization Methods for High-Dimensional Statistics
courses.description: The prevalence of high-dimensional data has motivated active research on efficient methods for tackling optimization problems that arise in statistical analysis. In this course, we will give an introduction to this exciting area of research, with emphasis on the theory of structured regularizers for high-dimensional statistics and the design and analysis of statistically and computationally efficient optimization algorithms. Applications in various areas of science and engineering, such as machine learning, signal processing, and statistics, will also be discussed. Students are expected to have taken ENGG 5501 or equivalent.

courses.learning_outcomes:
At the completion of this course, students should be able to
- understand the optimization formulations of various statistical problems
- understand various algorithmic approaches to statistical optimization problems
- analyze and implement basic statistical optimization algorithms

courses.subject: SEEM
courses.title: Optimal Control
courses.description: Dynamic continuous-time systems. Examples, modelling, and classification of optimal control problems. Pontryagin’s maximum principle: adjoint equation, Hamiltonian system, and sufficient condition of optimality. Bellman’s dynamic programming: principle of optimality, Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, and verification theorem. Linear quadratic control: Riccati equation and linear matrix inequality. Introduction to numerical methods of solving optimal control problems.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil-PhD Systems Engineering and Engineering Management
courses.academic_group: Div of System Erg & Erg Mgt
courses.academic_org: Div of System Erg & Erg Mgt
courses.course_syllabus: Optimal control theory deals with the search of a control policy for a given system to achieve optimality under certain criterion. This course focuses on dynamic stochastic control problems, in which agents make decisions under uncertainty dynamically. It introduces the stochastic control theory and computational methods in discrete time.
courses.recommended_readings:
1. Lecture notes
2. Dynamic Programming and Stochastic Control, Dimitri P. Bertsekas, 1976, Academic Press, New York
3. Stochastic Optimal Control: The Discrete-Time Case, Dimitri P. Bertsekas and Steven E. Shreve, 1978, Academic Press, New York
4. Stochastic Controls: Hamiltonian Systems and HJB Equations, Jiongmin Yong, Xun Yu Zhou, 1999, Springer, New York
5. Controlled Markov Processes and Viscosity Solutions, Wendell H. Fleming and H. Mete Soner, 2006, Springer, USA

courses.subject: SEEM
courses.title: Conversational Artificial Intelligence Systems
courses.description: Conversational AI is a rapidly developing, interdisciplinary field brings together speech processing, natural language processing, pattern recognition and machine learning. Conversational AI systems integrate a variety of speech and language processing technologies to bring about potentially life-changing applications. This course introduces students to the principles, theories and technologies in conversational AI. We build on fundamentals including signal processing, linguistics, information theory and machine learning. We introduce component technologies including automatic speech recognition, natural language understanding, dialog modeling, knowledge graph search, natural language generation, as well as text-to-speech synthesis. These technologies can be integrated into a diversity of systems, e.g. the ubiquitous chatbot systems, speech/text mining/retrieval/summarization systems, language learning systems, etc.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil-PhD Systems Engineering and Engineering Management
courses.academic_group: Div of System Erg & Erg Mgt
courses.academic_org: Div of System Erg & Erg Mgt
courses.learning_outcomes:
At the completion of the course, the student should have acquired the knowledge and ability relating to:
• Knowledge of different levels of description (namely, acoustic, phonetic and linguistic levels) of human speech and language,
• Understanding the component technologies for processing human speech and language at different levels,
• Understanding the AI technologies, such as automatic speech recognition, natural language understanding, dialog modeling, knowledge graph search, natural language generation, as well as text-to-speech synthesis,
• Develop different AI technologies and integrate them into different human speech and language systems,
• Develop end-to-end conversational AI systems.
courses.course_syllabus:
Human Speech Chain, Linguistic Hierarchy
Automatic Speech Recognition with Language Modeling
Natural Language Processing (shallow structures)
Natural Language Processing (deep structures)
Speech Understanding, Natural Language Understanding (embeddings)
Dialog modeling and discourse tracking in conversational dialogs
Knowledge graph search in support of interactive dialogs
Natural Language Generation (system-initiative, mixed-initiative, other types)
Concept-to-Speech Generation
Text-to-Speech Synthesis (emotive and expressive synthesis)
Other variations, e.g. machine translation systems, speech/text mining and retrieval systems, summarization systems

courses.subject: SEEM
courses.title: Advanced Models in Financial Engineering
courses.description: This course covers various applications of engineering technicalities in financial modeling. Emphasis will be on two main topics: investment portfolio optimization and financial derivative pricing. We introduce dynamic programming approach, martingale and PDE numerical solutions, Monte Carlo simulation methods for solving these two problems.

courses.academic_org: Div of System Erg & Erg Mgt
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Understanding the essences of stochastic calculus,
2. Understanding the no-arbitrage principle and fundamental theory of asset pricing,
3. Be able to use the tool of Ito calculus to build up financial pricing models,
4. Be able to carry out PDE and probabilistic approaches to evaluate financial securities.
courses.course_syllabus: The course introduces some basic concepts of stochastic calculus, an important mathematical tool used in financial engineering, and based on it, treats systematically the theory of risk neutral pricing. courses.subject: SEEM
courses.title: Text Mining Models and Application
courses.description: This course covers basic mining models that are able to discover useful patterns and knowledge from text data. The form of text data ranges from semi-structured representation to free natural language texts. It discusses retrieval models as well as learning models based on user feedback. It also covers advanced models including language modeling, automatic entity extraction, and machine learning models suitable for text. Text mining applications such as knowledge management are presented.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil-PhD Systems Engineering and Engineering Management
courses.academic_group: Div of System Erg & Erg Mgt
courses.academic_org: Div of System Erg & Erg Mgt
courses.learning_outcomes:
At the completion of the course, the student should have acquired the ability to understand
(i) techniques for text mining models
(ii) text data analytics
(iii) text mining applications
courses.course_syllabus: Massive amount of text data exist in electronic form such as news, emails, Web pages, memos, reports, etc. It generates a large demand for advanced techniques for retrieval and mining. The data typically ranges from semi-structured form (such as Web pages) to free texts (natural language texts). This course discusses methods for retrieving relevant text documents and analyzing text data based on machine learning approaches. Advanced models such as text classification, latent semantic indexing, topic modeling, neural network models will also be presented.
